This block can be used in conjunction with other physical signal blocks and custom blocks defined in the Simscape(TM) language to model other discrete and event-based behaviors.

blocks.name: PS Add
blocks.maskDescription:
This block adds signals of the two inputs:

y = u_1 + u_2

All connections are physical signal ports.

blocks.name: PS Bias
blocks.maskDescription:
This block adds a constant bias to the input physical signal:

y = u + bias

The Bias parameter value can be a scalar or a vector. The block output is a physical signal port.

blocks.name: PS Concatenate
blocks.maskDescription: Concatenates two input vectors or two-dimensional matrices into a single output. The two inputs must have commensurate units. The inputs are concatenated vertically by default. To concatenate horizontally, select the Concatenate horizontally check box.

blocks.name: PS Divide
blocks.maskDescription:
This block divides the first input signal by the second one:

y = u_1 ./ u_2

All connections are physical signal ports.

blocks.name: PS Dot Product
blocks.maskDescription:
Computes the dot product of two input vectors or two-dimensional matrices:

y = dot(u1,u2)

For two-dimensional matrix inputs, computes the column-wise dot product.

blocks.name: PS Gain
blocks.maskDescription:
This block multiplies the input physical signal by a constant:

y = u .* gain

The Gain parameter accepts both positive and negative values. All connections are physical signal ports.

blocks.name: PS Math Function
blocks.maskDescription:
This block applies a mathematical function to the input u:

y = fcn(u)

All connections are physical signal ports.

blocks.name: PS Product
blocks.maskDescription:
This block multiplies signals of the two inputs:

y = u_1 .* u_2

All connections are physical signal ports.

blocks.name: PS Subtract
blocks.maskDescription:
This block performs subtraction on two inputs:

y = u_1 - u_2

All connections are physical signal ports.

blocks.name: PS Sum of Elements
blocks.maskDescription:
Computes the sum of elements of the input vector or two-dimensional matrix:

y = sum(u)

For two-dimensional matrix inputs, computes the column-wise sum of elements. To compute the sum of all the elements of a matrix, select the Sum all elements check box.

blocks.name: PS Integrator
blocks.maskDescription: This block performs continuous-time integration of the input Physical Signal. The output resets to the initial condition when the optional reset signal, R, triggers. The initial condition can either be a fixed parameter or defined by a physical signal, X0. The output limits can either be fixed parameters or defined by physical signals, U and L.

blocks.name: PS State-Space
blocks.maskDescription:
This block implements a state-space representation of the linear time-invariant system that these equations define:
  E*dx/dt = A*x + B*u
  y = C*x + D*u
where x is the dimensionless state vector, u is the input vector, y is the output vector, E is the descriptor matrix, A is the state matrix, B is the input matrix, C is the output matrix, and D is the feedthrough or direct transmission matrix.

blocks.name: PS Transfer Function
blocks.maskDescription: This block implements a first-order transfer function. Select between a Lag or Lead-lag transfer function. The output resets to the initial condition when the optional reset signal, R, triggers. The initial condition can either be a fixed parameter or defined by a physical signal, Y0.

blocks.name: PS Lookup Table (1D)
blocks.maskDescription:
This block represents a physical signal converter whose input-output relationship is specified by a lookup table. The table grid must be in strictly ascending or strictly descending order, but the spacing can be nonuniform.

Use the Table button in the Plots section to visualize the table data based on the selected interpolation and extrapolation methods.

blocks.name: PS Lookup Table (2D)
blocks.maskDescription:
This block represents a physical signal converter whose input-output relationship is specified by a two-dimensional lookup table. The two table grid vectors define a Cartesian grid in 2D space. Each of the two table grid vectors must be in strictly ascending or strictly descending order, but the spacing can be nonuniform.

Use the Table button in the Plots section to visualize the table data based on the selected interpolation and extrapolation methods.

blocks.name: PS Lookup Table (3D)
blocks.maskDescription: This block represents a physical signal converter whose input-output relationship is specified by a three-dimensional lookup table. The three table grid vectors define a Cartesian grid in 3D space. Each of the three table grid vectors must be in strictly ascending or strictly descending order, but the spacing can be nonuniform.

blocks.name: PS Lookup Table (4D)
blocks.maskDescription: This block represents a physical signal converter whose input-output relationship is specified by a four-dimensional lookup table. The four table grid vectors define a Cartesian grid in 4D space. Each of the four table grid vectors must be in strictly ascending or strictly descending order, but the spacing can be nonuniform.

blocks.name: PS Scattered Lookup Table (2D)
blocks.referenceBlock: fl_lib/Physical Signals/Lookup Tables/PS Scattered Lookup Table (2D)
blocks.maskDescription: This block represents a physical signal converter whose input-output relationship is specified by a two-dimensional scattered lookup table. The data points coordinates 1 and 2 are vectors of unstructured data points in 2D space and the function values represent the data value at each of those points. All vectors must be the same size.

blocks.name: PS Scattered Lookup Table (3D)
blocks.referenceBlock: fl_lib/Physical Signals/Lookup Tables/PS Scattered Lookup Table (3D)
blocks.maskDescription: This block represents a physical signal converter whose input-output relationship is specified by a three-dimensional scattered lookup table. The data points coordinates 1, 2 and, 3 are vectors of unstructured data points in 3D space and the function values represent the data value at each of those points. All vectors must be the same size.

blocks.name: PS Abs
blocks.maskDescription:
This block returns the absolute value of its input:

y = abs(u)

All connections are physical signal ports.

blocks.name: PS Ceil
blocks.maskDescription:
This block returns the smallest integer larger than or equal to the input:

y = ceil(u)

All connections are physical signal ports.

blocks.name: PS Dead Zone
blocks.maskDescription:
This block generates zero output when input signal falls within a specified region, called a dead zone. The block parameters are the lower and upper limits of the dead zone. If the input is greater than or equal to the upper limit, the output is the input minus the upper limit. If the input is less than or equal to the lower limit, the output is the input minus the lower limit.

Both the input and the output are physical signal ports.

blocks.name: PS Fix
blocks.maskDescription:
This block rounds the input towards zero:

y = fix(u)

All connections are physical signal ports.

blocks.name: PS Floor
blocks.maskDescription:
This block returns the largest integer smaller than or equal to the input:

y = floor(u)

All connections are physical signal ports.

blocks.name: PS Max
blocks.maskDescription:
This block returns the maximum of its two input signals:

y = max(u_1,u_2)

All connections are physical signal ports.

blocks.name: PS Min
blocks.maskDescription:
This block returns the minimum of its two input signals:

y = min(u_1,u_2)

All connections are physical signal ports.

blocks.name: PS Round
blocks.maskDescription:
This block returns the nearest integer of the input:

y = round(u)

All connections are physical signal ports.

blocks.name: PS Saturation
blocks.maskDescription:
This block imposes upper and lower bounds on the output signal. When the input signal is within the range specified by the Lower limit and Upper limit parameters, the input signal passes through unchanged. When the input signal is outside these bounds, the signal is clipped to the upper or lower bound.

Both the input and the output are physical signal ports.

blocks.name: PS Selector
blocks.maskDescription: Select one or more elements from the input vector or two-dimensional matrix. The Indices parameter can be a scalar or vector of integers ranging from 1 to the number of elements in the input. The indices can be in any order, to enable construction of permutations and repeats.

blocks.name: PS Sign
blocks.maskDescription:
This block returns the sign of its input:

y = sign(u)

All connections are physical signal ports.

blocks.name: PS Switch
blocks.maskDescription: This block represents a switch. If the second input is greater than or equal to the threshold, then the output is connected to the first input. Otherwise, the output is connected to the third input.

blocks.name: PS Three-Element Demux
blocks.maskDescription: Splits a PS row vector of length three into three scalar physical signals.

blocks.name: PS Vector Norm
blocks.maskDescription:
Computes the Euclidean norm of the input vector or two-dimensional matrix:

y = sqrt(dot(u,u))

For two-dimensional matrix inputs, computes the column-wise vector norm.

blocks.name: PS Constant Offset Estimator
blocks.referenceBlock: fl_lib/Physical Signals/Periodic Operators/PS Constant Offset Estimator
blocks.maskDescription: This block measures the constant offset value of a periodic signal. This block requires a full period to provide meaningful results.

blocks.name: PS Harmonic Estimator (Amplitude, Phase)
blocks.referenceBlock: fl_lib/Physical Signals/Periodic Operators/PS Harmonic Estimator (Amplitude, Phase)
blocks.maskDescription: This block measures amplitude and phase of a single frequency component of a periodic signal. This block requires a full period to provide meaningful results.

blocks.name: PS Harmonic Estimator (Real, Imaginary)
blocks.referenceBlock: fl_lib/Physical Signals/Periodic Operators/PS Harmonic Estimator (Real, Imaginary)
blocks.maskDescription: This block measures real and imaginary parts of a single frequency component of a periodic signal. This block requires a full period to provide meaningful results.

blocks.name: PS RMS Estimator
blocks.maskDescription: This block measures root mean square (RMS) value of a periodic signal. This block requires a full period to provide meaningful results.

blocks.name: PS Terminator
blocks.maskDescription: Use this block to terminate physical signal outputs. Unconnected physical signal output ports do not generate warnings, but connection to a PS Terminator can be used to indicate that the signal was not inadvertently left unconnected

blocks.name: PS Constant
blocks.maskDescription:
This block creates a physical signal constant:

y = constant

The Constant parameter accepts both positive and negative values. The block output is a physical signal port.

blocks.name: PS Counter
blocks.maskDescription: This block counts up to the specified maximum value, then resets to the reset value. It starts counting at the initial value. Optionally the sample time parameter can be specified as a 1 by 2 row vector with the first element setting sample time, and the second setting sample time offset.

blocks.name: PS Ramp
blocks.maskDescription: This block creates a physical signal ramp. The output remains at the Initial output until the Start time, then increases based on the Slope. The units of Initial output and Slope multiplied by time must be commensurate. The block output is a physical signal port.

blocks.name: PS Random Number
blocks.maskDescription: This block provides a normally (Gaussian) distributed random number. The output is repeatable for a given seed. Optionally the sample time parameter can be specified as a 1 by 2 row vector with the first element setting sample time, and the second setting sample time offset.

blocks.name: PS Repeating Sequence
blocks.maskDescription: This block outputs a periodic piecewise linear signal. It outputs a constant initial value until time reaches the time offset. The linear segments are specified through their durations, start values and end values, however only the start values are required in the special cases where the signal is continuous or discrete.

blocks.name: PS Sine Wave
blocks.maskDescription:
This block creates a physical signal sine wave. The output follows the formula if Frequency specification is set to Frequency (SI):

O = amplitude * sin(2*pi*frequency * time + phase) + bias

If Frequency specification is set to Angular frequency, the formula is:

O = amplitude * sin(frequency * time + phase) + bias

The units of Amplitude and Bias must be commensurate. The block output is a physical signal port.

blocks.name: PS Step
blocks.maskDescription: This block creates a physical signal step function. The output remains constant until it steps instantaneously to a new value. The units of Initial value and Final value must be commensurate. The block output is a physical signal port.

blocks.name: PS Uniform Random Number
blocks.maskDescription: This block provides a uniformly distributed random number. The output is repeatable for a given seed. Optionally the sample time parameter can be specified as a 1 by 2 row vector with the first element setting sample time, and the second setting sample time offset.

blocks.name: PS Signal Specification
blocks.maskDescription:
This block explicitly specifies the size and unit of a physical signal.

Specify the signal size as 'zeros(m, n)'. Select a unit from the drop-down list, or type a unit name or unit expression.

blocks.name: Inertia (AB)
blocks.maskDescription:
This block represents an inertia that rotates around an axis.

Connections B and F are rigidly connected angle-based rotational conserving ports. Positive torque accelerates the inertia in the positive direction.

blocks.name: Inertia With Friction (AB)
blocks.maskDescription:
This block represents an inertia with friction that rotates around an axis.

Connections B and F are rigidly connected angle-based rotational conserving ports. Acceleration torque is the torque proportional to acceleration. Acceleration torque is positive when the inertia accelerates in the positive direction.

Disable frictional effects by setting the Breakaway friction coefficient, Coulomb friction coefficient, and Viscous friction coefficient to 0.

blocks.name: Initial Relative Angle (AB)
blocks.maskDescription:
This block provides an initial relative angle between ports B and F. Port F has a more positive angle than port B for positive relative angle. The relative angle may change during simulation. Specify the initial relative angle in the Initial Targets section.

Connections B and F are angle-based rotational conserving ports.

blocks.name: Rotational Damper (AB)
blocks.maskDescription:
This block represents an ideal rotational viscous damper.

Connections B and F are angle-based rotational conserving ports. The damper torque acts from port B on port F. Positive damper torque drives port F in the positive direction. Port F has a more positive angle than port B for positive relative angle.

blocks.name: Rotational Friction (AB)
blocks.maskDescription:
This block represents the resistive frictional contact between surfaces. Friction is the sum of Stribeck, Coulomb, and viscous components. Breakaway and Coulomb friction scale with normal force while viscous friction does not.

Connections B and F are angle-based rotational conserving ports. The friction torque acts from port B on port F. Positive friction torque drives port F in the positive direction. Port N is the optional physical signal port for specifying a variable normal force. Port F has a more positive angle than port B for positive relative angle.

blocks.name: Rotational Hard Stop (AB)
blocks.maskDescription:
This block represents a hard stop that restricts the relative angle of two bodies to greater than or equal to 0 rad. Contact between the two bodies is modeled either as a continuous spring and damper or as an instantaneous impulse based on a coefficient of restitution.

The spring-damper hard stop model can apply full stiffness and damping at the bound, or the torque can be applied smoothly through a transition region.

The instantaneous impact hard stop model lets the two bodies remain in contact if contact is reached at a relative rotational velocity smaller than the static contact speed threshold. The bodies remain in contact until a torque greater than the static contact release torque threshold is applied.

Connections B and F are angle-based rotational conserving ports. Relative angle, the angle of port F relative to port B, is less than or equal to zero when the hard stop is engaged. Torque acts from port B on port F. Positive torque drives port F in the positive direction and corresponds to an engaged hard stop.

blocks.name: Rotational Inerter (AB)
blocks.maskDescription:
This block represents an ideal rotational inerter. Torque is proportional to the rate of change of the relative angular velocity across the ports.

Connections B and F are angle-based rotational conserving ports. The inerter torque acts from port B on port F. Positive inerter torque drives port F in the positive direction. Port F has a more positive angle than port B for positive relative angle.

blocks.name: Rotational Spacer (AB)
blocks.maskDescription:
This block maintains a fixed relative angle between two angle-based rotational nodes. Relative angle is positive when port F has a more positive angle than port B.

Connections B and F are angle-based rotational conserving ports.

blocks.name: Rotational Spring (AB)
blocks.maskDescription:
This block represents an ideal spring with a linear relationship between torque and angular deformation.

Relative angle is the angle at port F minus the angle at port B. Deformation is defined as relative angle minus unloaded relative angle. The spring torque acts from port B on port F. Positive spring torque drives port F in the positive direction. The spring torque is positive for negative deformation. Connections B and F are angle-based rotational conserving ports.

Specify two variables as high priority targets. These high priority targets can be any variable pair besides torque and deformation. If the spring is in series with a known torque, then specify only relative angle or unloaded relative angle as a high priority target. If the spring is in parallel with a known relative angle, then specify only torque, deformation, or unloaded relative angle as a high priority target.

blocks.name: Rotational World (AB)
blocks.maskDescription: This block represents the stationary global reference frame. All angles in an angle-based rotational network are relative to this reference. All rotational ports connected to this block are stationary.

blocks.name: Rotational Motion Sensor (AB)
blocks.maskDescription:
This block measures absolute or relative angle, velocity, and acceleration in an angle-based rotational network. The sensor does not apply any torque on the network. Optionally wrap the measured angle over a 2π interval.

Connections B and F are angle-based rotational conserving ports. The physical signal ports α, ω, and θ report the rotational acceleration, velocity, and angle, respectively, of port F relative to port B. The measurement is positive when the motion at port F is greater than at port B. Optionally disable port B and measure motion with respect to the world frame.

blocks.name: Torque Sensor (AB)
blocks.maskDescription:
This block measures torque in an angle-based rotational network. Connect the sensor in series with a line to monitor the torque. There is no angle or angular velocity change across the sensor.

Connections B and F are angle-based rotational conserving ports. The physical signal port t reports the torque applied by the network at port B on the network at port F.

blocks.name: Angular Velocity Actuator (AB)
blocks.maskDescription:
This block represents an ideal actuator that maintains a specified relative angular velocity regardless of the load at the connected ports. The actuator has a relative angle between its ports.

Ports B and F are angle-based rotational conserving ports. Specify the relative angular velocity at physical signal port S. A positive signal indicates that the angular velocity at port F is greater than at port B. Port F has a more positive angle than port B for positive relative angle.

blocks.name: External Angular Velocity Source (AB)
blocks.maskDescription:
This block represents an ideal external angular velocity source that maintains a specified angular velocity at port R regardless of the load at the connected port.

Port R is an angle-based rotational conserving port. Specify the angular velocity at the physical signal port S.

blocks.name: External Torque Source (AB)
blocks.maskDescription:
This block represents an ideal external torque source that generates a specified torque regardless of the load or angular velocity at the connected port.

Port R is an angle-based rotational conserving port. Specify the torque at physical signal port S. A positive signal applies a positive torque on the network at port R.

blocks.name: Relative Angle Actuator (AB)
blocks.maskDescription:
This block represents an ideal actuator that maintains a specified angle between the connected ports regardless of the torque load at the ports.

Ports B and F are angle-based rotational conserving ports. The physical signal at port S specifies the angle between the ports. A positive signal indicates that port F has a more positive angle than port B.

blocks.name: Torque Actuator (AB)
blocks.maskDescription:
This block represents an ideal torque actuator that generates a specified torque regardless of the load or angular velocities at the ports. The actuator has a relative angle between its ports.

Ports B and F are angle-based rotational conserving ports. Specify the torque at physical signal port S. The torque acts from port B on port F. Positive torque drives port F in the positive direction. Port F has a more positive angle than port B for positive relative angle.

blocks.name: Interface (AB-Rotational)
blocks.maskDescription:
This block represents a rigid connection between an angle-based and non-angle-based rotational network. The rotational velocities at the ports are equal. The torques exerted by the networks on each other have equal magnitudes and opposite signs.

When the angle-based port is set to Bab, port Bab is an angle-based rotational port and port F is a non-angle-based rotational port. The interface torque acts from port Bab on port F. When the angle-based port is set to Fab, port B is a non-angle-based rotational port and port Fab is an angle-based rotational port. The interface torque acts from port B on port Fab.

blocks.name: Conductive Heat Transfer
blocks.maskDescription: This block models heat transfer in a thermal network by conduction through a layer of material. The rate of heat transfer is governed by Fourier's law and is proportional to the temperature difference, material thermal conductivity, area normal to the heat flow direction, and inversely proportional to the layer thickness. The thermal conductivity can be either variable or constant. If the thermal conductivity is variable, you can specify it either as a physical input signal at port K or as tabulated data versus temperature. If the thermal conductivity is specified using the physical signal, it remains at the Minimum thermal conductivity if the physical signal falls below this value.

blocks.name: Convective Heat Transfer
blocks.maskDescription: This block models heat transfer in a thermal network by convection due to fluid motion. The rate of heat transfer is proportional to the temperature difference, heat transfer coefficient, and surface area in contact with the fluid. The heat transfer coefficient can be either constant or variable. When the heat transfer coefficient is variable, specify it using the physical input signal at port K. If the heat transfer coefficient is variable, it remains at the Minimum heat transfer coefficient if the physical signal falls below this value.

blocks.name: Infinite Thermal Resistance
blocks.maskDescription: This block represents a break in a thermal network. There is no heat flow through the block regardless of the temperature difference. This block can also be used to set an initial value and priority for the temperature difference across port A and port B.

blocks.name: Perfect Insulator
blocks.maskDescription: This block represents a terminus in a thermal network with no heat flow and no energy storage. Use this block as an insulation for thermal conserving ports to prevent heat exchange with the environment and to model an adiabatic process. This block can also be used to set an initial value and priority for the temperature at the connected port.

blocks.name: Radiative Heat Transfer
blocks.maskDescription: This block models heat transfer in a thermal network by radiation between two surfaces. The rate of heat transfer is governed by the Stefan-Boltzmann law and is proportional to the difference in the fourth power of temperature, radiation coefficient, and surface area. The radiation coefficient depends on the geometric configuration and surface emissivities of the interacting bodies.

blocks.name: Thermal Mass
blocks.maskDescription: This block models internal energy storage in a thermal network. The rate of temperature increase is proportional to the heat flow rate into the material and inversely proportional to the mass and specific heat of the material. The mass of the block can be constant or variable. If the mass is variable, specify the change in mass using the physical input signal at port Mdot. When using variable mass, you must also specify the temperature of incoming mass using the physical input signal at port Tin. The temperature at port Tin only affects the results if the mass is increasing. If the mass is constant or decreasing, the temperature at port Tin has no effect.

blocks.name: Thermal Reference
blocks.maskDescription: This block represents a reference point in a thermal network where the temperature is equal to absolute zero.

blocks.name: Thermal Resistance
blocks.maskDescription: This block represents a generic resistance in a thermal network. The heat flow rate is proportional to the temperature difference and inversely proportional to the resistance.

blocks.name: Variable Thermal Resistance
blocks.maskDescription: This block represents a variable generic resistance in a thermal network. The heat flow rate is proportional to the temperature difference and inversely proportional to the resistance. The resistance is set by the physical signal port R. The resistance remains at the Minimum thermal resistance even if the physical signal falls below this value.

blocks.name: Heat Flow Rate Sensor
blocks.maskDescription: This block measures heat flow rate in a thermal network. There is no change in temperature across the sensor. The physical signal port H reports the heat flow rate through the sensor. The positive flow direction is from port A to port B.

blocks.name: Temperature Sensor
blocks.maskDescription: This block measures temperature in a thermal network. There is no heat flow through the sensor. The physical signal port T reports the temperature difference across the sensor. The measurement is positive when the temperature at port A is greater than the temperature at port B.

blocks.name: Controlled Temperature Source
blocks.maskDescription: This block represents an ideal energy source in a thermal network that can maintain a controlled temperature difference regardless of the heat flow rate. The temperature difference is set by the physical signal port S. A positive temperature difference causes the temperature at port B to be greater than the temperature at port A.

blocks.name: Controlled Heat Flow Rate Source
blocks.referenceBlock: fl_lib/Thermal/Thermal Sources/Controlled Heat Flow Rate Source
blocks.maskDescription: This block represents an ideal energy source in a thermal network that can maintain a controlled heat flow rate regardless of the temperature difference. The heat flow rate is set by the physical signal port S. A positive heat flow rate flows from port A to port B.

blocks.name: Heat Flow Rate Source
blocks.maskDescription: This block represents an ideal energy source in a thermal network that can maintain a constant heat flow rate regardless of the temperature difference. A positive heat flow rate flows from port A to port B.

blocks.name: Temperature Source
blocks.maskDescription: This block represents an ideal energy source in a thermal network that can maintain a constant absolute temperature at the port regardless of the heat flow rate.

blocks.name: Absolute Reference (TL)
blocks.maskDescription: This block represents the absolute reference in a thermal liquid network where pressure and temperature are equal to zero.

blocks.name: Cap (TL)
blocks.maskDescription: This block represents a terminus in a thermal liquid network. There is no mass or energy flow through the cap. This block can optionally be used to assign a beginning value and priority to the pressure and temperature of the connected node.

blocks.name: Constant Volume Chamber (TL)
blocks.maskDescription:
This block models mass and energy storage in a thermal liquid network. The chamber contains a constant volume of liquid. Pressure and temperature vary dynamically based on the net mass and energy accumulation in the volume.

Ports A, B, C, and D are the thermal liquid conserving ports associated with the chamber inlets. Port H is the thermal conserving port associated with the thermal mass of the liquid volume.

blocks.name: Flow Resistance (TL)
blocks.maskDescription: This block represents a generic pressure loss in a thermal liquid network. The drop in pressure is proportional to the square of the mass flow rate. The proportionality constant is determined from the specified nominal condition.

blocks.name: Infinite Flow Resistance (TL)
blocks.maskDescription:
This block represents a break in a thermal liquid network. There is no mass or energy flow through the break. However, the liquid properties, specified by the Thermal Liquid Settings (TL) block connected to the circuit, are the same on both sides of the break.

This block can optionally be used to assign a beginning value and priority to the differences in pressure and temperature of port A relative to port B.

blocks.name: Local Restriction (TL)
blocks.maskDescription: This block models the pressure loss due to a flow area restriction such as a valve or an orifice in a thermal liquid network. There is no heat exchange with the environment. The restriction area can be optionally set by the physical signal port AR [m^2]. The input is limited by the minimum and maximum restriction area.

blocks.name: Pipe (TL)
blocks.maskDescription:
This block models pipe flow dynamics in a thermal liquid network due to viscous friction losses and convective heat transfer with the pipe wall. You can optionally include the effects of dynamic compressibility and fluid inertia.

The pipe contains a constant volume of liquid. Temperature varies dynamically based on the net energy accumulation in the volume. Selecting Enable dynamic compressibility causes pressure to vary dynamically based on the net mass accumulation in the volume. Selecting Enable fluid inertia causes the liquid to resist acceleration.

Ports A and B are the thermal liquid conserving ports associated with the pipe inlet and outlet. Port H is the thermal conserving port associated with the pipe wall.

blocks.name: Reservoir (TL)
blocks.maskDescription: This block sets boundary conditions in a thermal liquid network. The volume of liquid inside the reservoir is assumed infinite. Therefore, the flow is assumed quasi-steady. Liquid leaves the reservoir at the reservoir pressure and temperature. Liquid enters the reservoir at the reservoir pressure, but its temperature is determined by the thermal liquid network upstream.  The reservoir pressure and temperature can be optionally set by physical signal ports P and T, respectively.

blocks.name: Rotational Mechanical Converter (TL)
blocks.maskDescription:
This block models an interface between a thermal liquid network and a mechanical rotational network. It can be used as a building block for rotary actuators.

The converter contains a variable volume of liquid. Temperature varies dynamically based on the net energy accumulation in the volume and the change in volume. Selecting Enable dynamic compressibility causes pressure to vary dynamically based on the additional mass accumulation in the volume beyond the change in volume.

Port A is the thermal liquid conserving port associated with the converter inlet. Port H is the thermal conserving port associated with the thermal mass of the liquid volume. Ports R and C are the mechanical rotational conserving ports associated with the moving interface and the converter casing, respectively. The rotation of port R relative to port C can be calculated internally or be set by the physical signal input port q. The rotation is defined to be zero when the liquid volume is equal to the dead volume.

blocks.name: Translational Mechanical Converter (TL)
blocks.maskDescription:
This block models an interface between a thermal liquid network and a mechanical translational network. It can be used as a building block for linear actuators.

The converter contains a variable volume of liquid. Temperature varies dynamically based on the net energy accumulation in the volume and the change in volume. Selecting Enable dynamic compressibility causes pressure to vary dynamically based on the additional mass accumulation in the volume beyond the change in volume.

Port A is the thermal liquid conserving port associated with the converter inlet. Port H is the thermal conserving port associated with the thermal mass of the liquid volume. Ports R and C are the mechanical translational conserving ports associated with the moving interface and the converter casing, respectively. The displacement of port R relative to port C can be calculated internally or be set by the physical signal input port p. The displacement is defined to be zero when the liquid volume is equal to the dead volume.

blocks.name: Flow Rate Sensor (TL)
blocks.maskDescription:
This block measures mass, volumetric, and energy flow rates in a thermal liquid network. There is no change in pressure or temperature across the sensor.

The physical signal ports M [kg/s], V [m^3/s], and φ [W] report the mass flow rate, the volumetric flow rate, and the energy flow rate, respectively, through the sensor. The positive flow direction is from port A to port B.

blocks.name: Pressure & Temperature Sensor (TL)
blocks.maskDescription:
This block measures pressure and temperature in a thermal liquid network. There is no mass or energy flow through the sensor.

The physical signal ports P, Pa, and Pg [Pa] report the pressure difference across the sensor, the absolute pressure at port A, and the gauge pressure at port A, respectively. The physical signal port T [K] reports the temperature at port A or across the sensor. Difference measurements are positive when the values at port A are greater than port B.

blocks.name: Thermodynamic Properties Sensor (TL)
blocks.maskDescription:
This block measures thermodynamic fluid states in a thermal liquid network. There is no mass or energy flow through the sensor.

The physical signal ports u [kJ/kg], ρ [kg/m^3], and cp [kJ/(kg*K)] report the specific internal energy, density, and specific heat at constant pressure, respectively, measured at port A.

blocks.name: Transport Properties Sensor (TL)
blocks.maskDescription:
This block measures transport properties in a thermal liquid network. There is no mass or energy flow through the sensor.

The physical signal ports μ, ν, k, and Pr report the dynamic viscosity, kinematic viscosity, thermal conductivity, and prandtl number, respectively, measured at port A.

blocks.name: Flow Rate Source (TL)
blocks.maskDescription: This block represents an ideal mechanical energy source in a thermal liquid network that can maintain a constant or controlled mass flow rate or volumetric flow rate regardless of the pressure differential. There is no flow resistance and no heat exchange with the environment. A positive value causes liquid to flow from port A to port B.

blocks.name: Pressure Source (TL)
blocks.maskDescription: This block represents an ideal mechanical energy source in a thermal liquid network that can maintain a constant or controlled pressure differential regardless of the mass flow rate. There is no flow resistance and no heat exchange with the environment. The pressure differential can be optionally set by the physical signal port P. A positive pressure differential causes the pressure at port B to be greater than port A.

blocks.name: Thermal Liquid Settings (TL)
blocks.maskDescription:
This block provides liquid properties to the connected thermal liquid network. The liquid properties can be specified as two-dimensional tables or one-dimensional vectors. For the two-dimensional liquid property tables, rows correspond to Temperature vector and Columns correspond to Pressure vector. The one-dimensional liquid property vectors correspond to Temperature vector. The default liquid is water.

Use the Thermal liquid properties button in the Plots section to visualize the provided liquid properties.

blocks.name: Initial Length (PB)
blocks.maskDescription:
This block provides an initial length between ports B and F. The length may change during simulation. Specify the initial length by setting the Length variable in the Initial Targets section.

Connections B and F are position-based translational conserving ports. Port F has a more positive position than port B for positive length.

blocks.name: Mass (PB)
blocks.maskDescription:
This block represents a point mass with gravitational effects that moves along an inclined rail. Gravity can induce motion along the rail. The Mechanical Translational Properties block specifies the gravitational acceleration and rail inclination in the network.

Connection R is a position-based translational conserving port. Port force is the force exerted by other position-based translational blocks on this block. Acceleration force is positive when the mass accelerates in the positive direction.

blocks.name: Mass With Friction (PB)
blocks.maskDescription:
This block represents a mass with friction and gravitational effects that moves along an inclined rail. Gravity can induce motion along the rail. Gravity and an optional additional normal force induce friction with the stationary rail. The Mechanical Translational Properties block specifies the gravitational acceleration and rail inclination in the network.

Connection R is a position-based translational conserving port. Port force is the force exerted by other position-based translational blocks on this block. Acceleration force is positive when the mass accelerates in the positive direction.

Disable frictional effects by setting the Breakaway friction coefficient, Coulomb friction coefficient, and Viscous friction coefficient to 0.

blocks.name: Mass With Length (PB)
blocks.maskDescription:
This block represents a mass with length and gravitational effects that moves along an inclined rail. Gravity can induce motion along the rail. The Mechanical Translational Properties block specifies the gravitational acceleration and rail inclination in the network.

Connections B and F are position-based translational conserving ports. Port F has a more positive position than port B for positive length. Acceleration force is positive when the mass accelerates in the positive direction.

blocks.name: Mass With Length & Friction (PB)
blocks.maskDescription:
This block represents a mass with length, gravitational effects, and friction that moves along an inclined rail. Gravity can induce motion along the rail. Gravity and an optional additional normal force induce friction with the stationary rail. The Mechanical Translational Properties block specifies the gravitational acceleration and rail inclination in the network.

Acceleration force is positive when the mass accelerates in the positive direction.

Connections B and F are position-based translational conserving ports. Port F has a more positive position than port B for positive length.

Disable frictional effects by setting the Breakaway friction coefficient, Coulomb friction coefficient, and Viscous friction coefficient to 0.

blocks.name: Translational Friction (PB)
blocks.maskDescription:
This block represents the resistive frictional contact between surfaces. Friction is the sum of Stribeck, Coulomb, and viscous components. Breakaway and Coulomb friction scale with normal force while viscous friction does not.

Connections B and F are position-based translational conserving ports. Port F has a more positive position than port B for positive length. The friction force acts from port B on port F. Positive friction force drives port F in the positive direction. Port N is the optional physical signal port for specifying a variable normal force.

blocks.name: Translational Damper (PB)
blocks.maskDescription:
This block represents an ideal viscous damper.

Connections B and F are position-based translational conserving ports. Port F has a more positive position than port B for positive length. The force corresponds to the damper in a state of compression when length is positive.

blocks.name: Translational Hard Stop (PB)
blocks.maskDescription:
This block represents a hard stop that restricts the relative position of two bodies to greater than or equal to 0 m. Contact between the two bodies is modeled either as a continuous spring and damper or as an instantaneous impulse based on a coefficient of restitution.

The spring-damper hard stop model can apply full stiffness and damping at the bound, or the force can be applied smoothly through a transition region.

The instantaneous impact hard stop model lets the two bodies remain in contact if contact is reached at a velocity smaller than the static contact speed threshold. The bodies remain in contact until a force greater than the static contact release force threshold is applied.

Connections B and F are position-based translational conserving ports. Port F has a more positive position than port B for positive gap length. Gap length is less than or equal to zero when the hard stop is engaged. Force acts from port B on port F. Positive force drives port F in the positive direction and corresponds to an engaged hard stop.

blocks.name: Translational Spacer (PB)
blocks.maskDescription:
This block maintains a fixed length between two position-based mechanical translational nodes. Length is positive when port F has a more positive position than port B.

Connections B and F are position-based translational conserving ports. The spacer force acts from port B on port F. Positive spacer force drives port F in the positive direction. Positive spacer force corresponds to the spacer in a state of compression when length is positive.

blocks.name: Translational Spring (PB)
blocks.maskDescription:
This block represents an ideal mechanical linear spring.

Deformation is defined as Length - Rest length. The spring force is positive for negative deformation. Positive spring force corresponds to the spring in a state of compression when length is positive.

The spring force acts from port B on port F. Positive spring force drives port F in the positive direction. Connections B and F are position-based translational conserving ports. Port F has a more positive position than port B for positive length.

Specify two variables as high priority targets. These high priority targets can be any variable pair besides force and deformation. If the spring is in series with a known force, specify only length or rest length as a high priority target. If the spring is in parallel with a known length, specify only force, deformation, or rest length as a high priority target.

blocks.name: Translational World (PB)
blocks.maskDescription: This block represents the stationary global reference frame. All positions in a position-based translational network are relative to this reference. All translational ports connected to this block are stationary.

blocks.name: Force Sensor (PB)
blocks.maskDescription:
This block measures force in a position-based translational network. Connect the sensor in series with a line to monitor the force. There is no position or velocity change across the sensor.

Connections B and F are position-based translational conserving ports. The physical signal port f reports the force applied by the network at port B on the network at port F.

blocks.name: Translational Motion Sensor (PB)
blocks.maskDescription:
This block measures absolute or relative position, velocity, and acceleration in a position-based translational network. The sensor does not apply any force on the network.

Connections B and F are position-based translational conserving ports. The physical signal ports P, V, and A report the measured position, velocity, and acceleration, respectively, of port F relative to port B. The measurement is positive when the motion at port F is greater than at port B. Optionally disable port B and measure motion with respect to the world frame.

blocks.name: External Translational Velocity Source (PB)
blocks.maskDescription:
This block represents an ideal external velocity source that maintains a specified velocity at port R regardless of the load at the port.

Port R is a position-based translational conserving port. Specify the velocity at the physical signal port S.

blocks.name: External Force Source (PB)
blocks.maskDescription:
This block represents an ideal external force source that generates a specified force regardless of the load or velocity at the connected port.

Port R is a position-based translational conserving port. Specify the force at physical signal port S. A positive signal applies a positive force on the network at port R.

blocks.name: Force Actuator (PB)
blocks.maskDescription:
This block represents an ideal force actuator with length that generates a specified force regardless of the load or velocities at the ports.

Ports B and F are position-based translational conserving ports. Specify the force at physical signal port S. A positive signal applies a force that acts to separate the ports when length is positive. Port F has a more positive position than port B for positive length.

blocks.name: Length Actuator (PB)
blocks.maskDescription:
This block represents an ideal actuator that maintains a specified length regardless of the load at the connected ports.

Ports B and F are position-based translational conserving ports. The physical signal at port S specifies the distance between the ports. A positive signal indicates that port F has a more positive position than port B.

blocks.name: Translational Velocity Actuator (PB)
blocks.maskDescription:
This block represents an ideal velocity actuator with length that maintains a specified velocity regardless of the load at the connected ports.

Ports B and F are position-based translational conserving ports. Specify the relative velocity at physical signal port S. A positive signal indicates that the velocity at port F is greater than at port B. Port F has a more positive position than port B for positive length.

blocks.name: Interface (PB-Translational)
blocks.maskDescription:
This block represents a rigid connection between a position-based and non-position-based mechanical translational network. The velocities at the ports are equal. The forces exerted by the networks on each other have equal magnitudes and opposite signs.

When the Position-based port is set to Bpb, port Bpb is a position-based translational port and port F is non-position-based translational port. The interface force acts from port Bpb on port F. When the Position-based port is set to Fpb, port B is a non-position-based translational port and port Fpb is position-based translational port. The interface force acts from port B on port Fpb.

blocks.name: Mechanical Translational Properties (PB)
blocks.maskDescription:
This block provides gravitational acceleration to the connected translational network. Gravity, g, acts downwards. Incline angle, β, is the angle of the network's positive direction relative to the horizontal. The network positive direction has an upward slope for angles between β and 180 degrees and a downward slope for angles between 0 and -180 degrees.

g*sin(β) is the component of gravity acting along the network. Positive g*sin(β) corresponds to a positive incline angle that induces motion in the negative direction along the rail.

g*|cos(β)| is the component of gravity acting perpendicular to the rail that induces normal force between mass and the rail.

blocks.name: Absolute Reference (2P)
blocks.maskDescription: This block represents the absolute reference in a two-phase fluid network where pressure and specific internal energy are equal to zero.

blocks.name: Cap (2P)
blocks.maskDescription: This block represents a terminus in a two-phase fluid network. There is no mass or energy flow through the cap. This block can optionally be used to assign a beginning value and priority to the pressure and specific internal energy of the connected node.

blocks.name: Constant Volume Chamber (2P)
blocks.maskDescription:
This block models mass and energy storage in a two-phase fluid network. The chamber contains a constant volume of fluid. Pressure and specific internal energy vary dynamically based on the net mass and energy accumulation in the volume.

Ports A, B, C, and D are the two-phase fluid conserving port associated with the chamber inlets. Port H is the thermal conserving port associated with the thermal mass of the fluid volume.

blocks.name: Flow Resistance (2P)
blocks.maskDescription: This block represents a generic pressure loss in a two-phase fluid network. The drop in pressure is proportional to the square of the mass flow rate and to the specific volume. The proportionality constant is determined from the specified nominal condition. Set Nominal specific volume to zero to omit the density dependence.

blocks.name: Infinite Flow Resistance (2P)
blocks.maskDescription:
This block represents a break in a two-phase fluid network. There is no mass or energy flow through the break. However, the fluid properties, specified by the Two-Phase Fluid Properties (2P) block connected to the circuit, are the same on both sides of the break.

This block can optionally be used to assign a beginning value and priority to the differences in pressure and specific internal energy of port A relative to port B.

blocks.name: Local Restriction (2P)
blocks.maskDescription: This block models the pressure loss due to a flow area restriction such as a valve or an orifice in a two-phase fluid network. There is no heat exchange with the environment. The restriction area can be optionally set by the physical signal port AR. The input is limited by the minimum and maximum restriction area.

blocks.name: Pipe (2P)
blocks.maskDescription:
This block models pipe flow dynamics in a two-phase fluid network due to viscous friction losses and convective heat transfer with the pipe wall. You can optionally include the effects of fluid inertia.

The pipe contains a constant volume of fluid. Pressure and specific internal energy vary dynamically based on the net mass and energy accumulation in the volume. Selecting Enable fluid inertia causes the fluid to resist acceleration.

Ports A and B are the two-phase fluid conserving ports associated with the pipe inlet and outlet. Port H is the thermal conserving port associated with the pipe wall.

blocks.name: Reservoir (2P)
blocks.maskDescription:
This block sets boundary conditions in a two-phase fluid network. The volume of fluid inside the reservoir is assumed infinite. Therefore, the flow is assumed quasi-steady. Fluid leaves the reservoir at the reservoir pressure and specific internal energy. Fluid enters the reservoir at the reservoir pressure, but the specific internal energy is determined by the two-phase fluid network upstream.

The reservoir pressure, condensing temperature, or evaporating temperature is optionally set by the physical signal port P, Tc, or Te, respectively. The reservoir temperature, vapor quality, vapor void fraction, specific enthalpy, specific internal energy, subcooling, or superheating is optionally set by the physical signal port T, X, a, H, U, SC, or SH, respectively.

blocks.name: Rotational Mechanical Converter (2P)
blocks.maskDescription:
This block models an interface between a two-phase fluid network and a mechanical rotational network. It can be used as a building block for rotary actuators.

The converter contains a variable volume of fluid. Pressure and specific internal energy vary based on the net mass and energy accumulation in the volume and the change in volume.

Port A is the two-phase fluid conserving port associated with the converter inlet. Port H is the thermal conserving port associated with the thermal mass of the fluid volume. Ports R and C are the mechanical rotational conserving ports associated with the moving interface and converter casing, respectively. The rotation of port R relative to port C can be calculated internally or be set by the physical signal input port q. The rotation is defined to be zero when the liquid volume is equal to the dead volume.

blocks.name: Translational Mechanical Converter (2P)
blocks.maskDescription:
This block models an interface between a two-phase fluid network and a mechanical translational network. It can be used as a building block for linear actuators.

The converter contains a variable volume of fluid. Pressure and specific internal energy vary based on the net mass and energy accumulation in the volume and the change in volume.

Port A is the two-phase fluid conserving port associated with the converter inlet. Port H is the thermal conserving port associated with the thermal mass of the fluid volume. Ports R and C are the mechanical translational conserving ports associated with the moving interface and the converter casing, respectively. The displacement of port R relative to port C can be calculated internally or be set by the physical signal input port p. The displacement is defined to be zero when the liquid volume is equal to the dead volume.

blocks.name: Flow Rate Sensor (2P)
blocks.maskDescription:
This block measures mass, volumetric, and energy flow rates in a two-phase fluid network. There is no change in pressure or specific internal energy across the sensor.

The physical signal ports M [kg/s], V [m^3/s], and φ [kW] report the mass flow rate, the volumetric flow rate, and the energy flow rate, respectively, through the sensor. The positive flow direction is from port A to port B.

blocks.name: Pressure, Temperature & Internal Energy Sensor (2P)
blocks.referenceBlock: fl_lib/Two-Phase Fluid/Sensors/Pressure, Temperature & Internal Energy Sensor (2P)
blocks.maskDescription:
This block measures pressure and specific internal energy in a two-phase fluid network. There is no mass or energy flow through the sensor.

The physical signal ports P, Pa, and Pg [MPa] report the pressure difference across the sensor, the absolute pressure at port A, and the gauge pressure at port A, respectively. The physical signal ports T [K] and U [kJ/kg] report the temperature and specific internal energy, respectively at port A or across the sensor. The measurements are positive when the values at port A are greater than the values at port B.

blocks.name: Saturation Properties Sensor (2P)
blocks.maskDescription:
This block measures saturated thermodynamic fluid states based on the pressure or temperature in a two-phase fluid network. There is no mass or energy flow through the sensor.

The physical signal ports TL and TV [K], UL and UV [kJ/kg], HL and HV [kJ/kg], VL and VV [m^3/kg], and rhoL and rhoV [kg/m^3] report the saturated liquid and saturated vapor temperature, specific internal energy, specific enthalpy, specific volume, and density, respectively, based on the pressure measured at port A. The physical signal ports PL and PV [MPa] report the saturated liquid and saturated vapor pressure, respectively, based on the temperature measured at port A.

blocks.name: Thermodynamic Properties Sensor (2P)
blocks.maskDescription:
This block measures thermodynamic fluid states in a two-phase fluid network. There is no mass or energy flow through the sensor.

The physical signal ports T [K], h [kJ/kg], ρ [kg/m^3], v [m^3/kg], and s [kJ/(kg*K)] report the temperature, specific enthalpy, density, specific volume, and specific entropy, respectively, measured at port A.

blocks.name: Transport Properties Sensor (2P)
blocks.maskDescription:
This block measures transport properties in a two-phase fluid network. There is no mass or energy flow through the sensor.

The physical signal ports μ, ν, k, and Pr report the dynamic viscosity, kinematic viscosity, thermal conductivity, and Prandtl number, respectively, measured at port A.

blocks.name: Vapor Quality Sensor (2P)
blocks.maskDescription:
This block measures the mixture vapor fraction in a two-phase fluid network. There is no mass or energy flow through the sensor.

The physical signal port X reports the vapor quality or the vapor void fraction measured at port A. When pressure is greater than or equal to the critical pressure, vapor quality or vapor void fraction is undefined and port X reports a value of -1.

blocks.name: Flow Rate Source (2P)
blocks.maskDescription: This block represents an ideal mechanical energy source in a two-phase fluid network that can maintain a constant or controlled mass flow rate or volumetric flow rate regardless of the pressure differential. There is no flow resistance and no heat exchange with the environment. A positive value causes fluid to flow from port A to port B.

blocks.name: Pressure Source (2P)
blocks.maskDescription: This block represents an ideal mechanical energy source in a two-phase fluid network that can maintain a constant or controlled pressure differential regardless of the mass flow rate. There is no flow resistance and no heat exchange with the environment. The pressure differential can be optionally set by the physical signal port P. A positive pressure differential causes the pressure at port B to be greater than port A.

blocks.name: Two-Phase Fluid Properties (2P)
blocks.maskDescription:
This block provides fluid properties to the connected two-phase fluid network. The fluid property tables are two-dimensional arrays in which the rows correspond to the Normalized liquid internal energy vector or the Normalized vapor internal energy vector and the columns correspond to the Pressure vector. The Saturated liquid specific internal energy vector and the Saturated vapor specific internal energy vector are one-dimensional arrays with the same length as the Pressure vector.

If the Pressure vector extends above the Critical pressure, the corresponding elements of the Saturated liquid specific internal energy vector and of the Saturated vapor specific internal energy vector can represent any curve or line extending above the critical point.

Use the Fluid properties button in the Plots section to visualize the specified fluid properties as a function of pressure and specific internal energy or specific enthalpy for the connected two-phase fluid network.
